name: Kerrville Folk Festival
dates: 18 days annually in late May and early June; 2027 passes went on sale in November 2026
customer: Songwriters, folk fans, campers and travelers who want to join a temporary music community
unique: Quiet Valley Ranch becomes an 18-day village of songwriter concerts, campground jam sessions and all-ages activities, founded by Rod Kennedy and still run by a member-supported nonprofit.
buzz: Regulars buy discounted passes before the lineup is announced. The campfire songs after the main stage show are as much of the draw as the scheduled concerts.

name: Crider's Rodeo and Dancehall
cost: $15 combo; $10 for active military and seniors; ages 12 and under free
dates: Saturday nights from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend; rodeo at 8 p.m. and live music from 9 p.m. to 1 a.m.
customer: Families, ranch people, dancers and visitors who want a summer night beside the Guadalupe
unique: An open-air rodeo and dance floor overlook the South Fork of the Guadalupe, growing from Walter and Audrey Crider's 1925 school fundraiser into a weekly summer ritual.
buzz: Summer regulars describe it as a place that stays familiar as they return with children and grandchildren. The rodeo leads into four hours of live country dancing.

name: Kerrville Kayak and Canoe River Trips
cost: $35 half-day or $60 full day for a single kayak or paddleboard
dates: Shop Tuesday to Saturday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.; reservations recommended and river levels permitting; winter break Christmas Eve to Valentine's Day
customer: Paddlers, fishing travelers and small groups seeking upper Guadalupe access with local logistics
unique: The local outfitter runs half-day single-kayak river trips with a shuttle and also rents canoes, kayaks and paddleboards for pickup at its Broadway shop.
buzz: The September 29, 2026 update says flood damage closed both park concessions, but shop rentals, shuttles and arranged equipment service at Flat Rock Park's open boat ramp remain available.

name: Kerrville-Schreiner Park
cost: $8 adults; $4 children and seniors; veterans and military free with identification
dates: Daily, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; river access and beachfront closed until further notice after the July 2026 flood
company: City of Kerrville Parks and Recreation
customer: Hikers, mountain bikers, campers and families who want a large Hill Country park close to town
unique: A 517-acre former state park with more than 12 miles of multiuse trails, hillside and riverside camping areas, cabins, a playground and a pollinator garden on the Guadalupe.
buzz: The trails, day-use areas and campsites are open during flood recovery. Current visitors should come for the hills rather than expecting river access.

name: Museum of Western Art
dates: Tuesday to Saturday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.
customer: Art travelers, Western history readers and families with children
unique: Contemporary paintings and bronzes of the American West fill the last public building designed by Texas architect O'Neil Ford, with a separate children's gallery.
buzz: Visitors come for cowboy art and leave talking about the building, the courtyard bronzes and the changing exhibitions.

name: Stonehenge II at Hill Country Arts Foundation
dates: Daily, dawn to dusk, except during the Texas Arts and Crafts Fair on the last weekend of September
customer: Roadside oddity collectors, photographers and families driving the Guadalupe River valley
unique: A roughly 90 percent scale Stonehenge replica and two Easter Island heads stand in a field on an active arts campus beside the Guadalupe River.
buzz: People treat it as a quick, absurd photo stop, then discover that the surrounding foundation also stages theater and art programs.

name: The Coming King Sculpture Prayer Garden
dates: Daily, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., weather permitting
customer: Road trippers, sculpture viewers, pilgrims and anyone curious about monumental religious art
unique: A 77-foot-7-inch hollow steel cross rises over a 24.5-acre hilltop garden of monumental Christian sculptures, prayer rocks and scripture tiles beside Interstate 10.
buzz: Even visitors with no religious connection stop for the scale of the cross and the open hilltop setting. Admission is always free.

name: Camp Verde General Store and Restaurant
dates: Store daily, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; restaurant daily, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.; closed major holidays
company: Camp Verde General Store and Restaurant
customer: History travelers, breakfast and lunch diners, and shoppers looking for regional jams and sauces
unique: A store established to serve Fort Verde in 1857 now occupies a stone building near Verde Creek, with a restaurant and a 10-foot camel sculpture recalling the Army's local camel experiment.
buzz: Visitors ask for the menu's account of the camel experiment, browse the packed store and make breakfast or lunch part of the stop rather than just a quick photo.

name: Y.O. Ranch Headquarters History and Wildlife Tour
cost: $95 per person for a group of 10 or more; $145 per person for a private tour
dates: Daily tours by reservation; private tours at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.
customer: Wildlife photographers, animal watchers and travelers interested in the workings and history of a Texas game ranch
unique: A guided two-hour drive crosses a working Hill Country ranch with more than 30 species of exotic wildlife and historic cabins dating to the 1880s.
buzz: Guides combine close views of animals such as giraffes, zebras, blackbuck and aoudad with ranch history and conservation interpretation.

name: Hill Country Shooting Sports Center
cost: $12 range fee reported in May 2026; ammunition and other costs extra
dates: Wednesday to Saturday, 9 a.m. to 7 p.m.; Sunday, noon to 7 p.m.; closes at dark when earlier
company: Hill Country Shooting Sports Center, Inc.
customer: Firearms owners, clay target shooters and travelers who want to try a public Olympic training venue
unique: The 140-acre public range is an official United States Olympic Training Site, with sporting clays, international bunker trap, skeet, five-stand, rifle and pistol options.
buzz: Recent reviewers single out the knowledgeable staff and the chance to shoot on the same grounds used for national team training and competition.
